response: Happy to explain the tradeoffs. On-ear headphones rest on the ears and are usually lighter and more portable, but their lighter seal often means weaker noise cancellation and more sound leakage than over-ear models. Over-ear headphones fully enclose the ears, giving the best passive isolation and typically the strongest noise cancellation and comfort for long sessions, though they're bulkier and can get warm. In-ear/true wireless earbuds are the most portable and can have excellent active noise cancellation, but fit and comfort vary and some people find them less comfortable for extended wear. For maximum noise-canceling effect, over-ear generally wins; for comfort and portability, on-ear or earbuds may suit you better.
